1.note: The author is introducing a new event in order to begin his history of the kings of Israel. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

The author is using one part of the Philistines, their **face**, to mean all of them in the act of attacking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the attacking Philistines]

2.note: See the discussion in the introduction to 1 Chronicles of how the author may use the term **struck** not to mean that someone merely hit a person but to mean that someone killed that person. Alternate translation: [And the Philistines killed]

3.note: The author is speaking of the **battle** as if it had been a **heavy** physical weight pressing down on Saul. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the Philistines fought fiercely against Saul]

Since the term **shooters** could describe either soldiers throwing javelins or soldiers launching arrows, the author adds the phrase **with the bow** to clarify his meaning. Your language may have a single term that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [And the archers … from the archers]

By this phrase, the author means that Saul was in great pain because the archers had wounded him with arrows. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And he writhed in pain because the archers had wounded him with arrows]

4.q: שְׁלֹ֥ף חַרְבְּ⁠ךָ֣ ׀ וְ⁠דָקְרֵ֣⁠נִי בָ֗⁠הּ פֶּן־יָבֹ֜אוּ הָ⁠עֲרֵלִ֤ים הָ⁠אֵ֨לֶּה֙ וְ⁠הִתְעַלְּלוּ־בִ֔⁠י
4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [So that these uncircumcised ones do not come and abuse me, draw your sword and stab me with it]

Saul is using the adjective **uncircumcised** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. He is using this as a term of derision to mean people who do not worship Yahweh. Your language may have a comparable term of derision that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [these heathen] or [these uncircumcised Philistines]

By **abuse**, Saul means that the Philistines would taunt and torture him. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and taunt and torture me]

4.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א אָבָה֙ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֔י⁠ו כִּ֥י יָרֵ֖א מְאֹ֑ד
4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [But since the carrier of his equipment feared greatly, he was not willing]
By **the sword**, the author means Saul’s own sword. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation, as in the UST, if that would be helpful to your readers.

6.note: The phrase **all of his house** could mean: (1) all the adult sons who could reasonably have succeeded Saul as king. In that case, **house** would mean “dynasty.” The author of 1 Chronicles does not describe the civil war between David and Saul’s youngest son Ish-bosheth (whom he calls Esh Baal in 9:49). Instead, he proceeds directly to the story of how the Israelites asked David to be their king at the end of that civil war. From his perspective, Saul’s dynasty effectively ended when he and his adult sons died in this battle. Alternate translation: [and his three adult sons who could have succeeded him as king died with him] or (2) as a generalization, all of the Israelite soldiers who were fighting together with Saul, that is, his sons and his bodyguard. That is the meaning of the similar phrase “all his men” in the parallel passage in 1 Samuel 31:6. Alternate translation: [and three of his sons and all of his bodyguard died together]

7.note: Here the masculine term **men** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [And all of the people of Israel]

By **the valley**, the author means the territory north of the Valley of Jezreel and west of the Jordan River, as the parallel passage in 1 Samuel 31:7 makes clear. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in the territory north of the Valley of Jezreel and west of the Jordan River]

The pronoun **they** refers to the Israelite soldiers who survived the battle with the Philistines. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the surviving Israelite soldiers had fled]

8.note: The author is using this phrase to introduce a new development in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method here that is natural in your language for introducing a new development.

The author is using the adjective **slain** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [those whom they had killed]

The author is using the term **fallen** to represent having died in battle, since soldiers fall down when they die. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [dead]

9.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And they sent messengers into the land of the Philistines all around to proclaim the news of their victory]

The author means that the messengers announced the news of the victory in the temples of the idols that the Philistines worshiped. Since the idols were not real gods and could not hear or understand this news, you may wish to say in your translation that this is what the Philistines actually did, as in 1 Samuel 31:9. Alternate translation: [to proclaim in the temple of their idols and to the people]

10.note: The author is speaking of the main temple in which the Philistines worshiped their idols as if it were a **house** in which those idols lived. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the temple of their gods … in the temple of Dagon]

11.note: The author is saying **all** as a generalization for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [And people throughout Jabesh Gilead heard]

12.note: Here the term **arose** means that these **men** took action. It does not mean merely that they stood up from a sitting or reclining position. If this expression does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And all of the men of valor took action]

The author is saying **all** as an overstatement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [And together their men of valor]

The author assumes that readers will know that the Philistines had fastened these **corpses** to the wall of the city of Beth Shan, as 1 Samuel 31:10 says explicitly. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the corpse of Saul and the corpses of his sons, which the Philistines had fastened to the wall of Beth Shan]

The people of Jabesh Gilead **fasted seven days** to show respect to Saul and to express their grief over his death. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action. Alternate translation: [And they fasted seven days as a sign of mourning and respect]

13.q: וַ⁠יָּ֣מָת שָׁא֗וּל בְּ⁠מַֽעֲל⁠וֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָעַ֣ל בַּֽ⁠יהוָ֔ה עַל־דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־שָׁמָ֑ר וְ⁠גַם־לִ⁠שְׁא֥וֹל בָּ⁠א֖וֹב לִ⁠דְרֽוֹשׁ
13.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [And because of his transgression that he transgressed against Yahweh, because of the word of Yahweh that he did not keep, and also for having inquired of a ritual pit for seeking, Saul died]

The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [because of the sin that he committed against Yahweh]

The author is speaking as if the **word** of Yahweh (that is, a command that Yahweh spoke to Saul) were an object that Saul could have kept somewhere. To describe this aspect of Saul’s **transgression**, he is referring to the episode related in 1 Samuel 15:1–29, in which Saul disobeys a direct command of Yahweh and the prophet Samuel tells him that Yahweh will make someone else the king of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly, and you could refer your readers to the passage in 1 Samuel in a footnote. Alternate translation: [because of the command of Yahweh that he did not obey]

To describe this further aspect of Saul’s **transgression**, the author is referring to the episode related in 1 Samuel 26:3–19, in which Saul goes to a medium for guidance and Samuel tells him that because of his disobedience, he is going to die in battle the next day. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could refer them to this passage in 1 Samuel in a footnote.

14.note: Here the term **For** introduces not a reason but an explanation. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. In some languages it may not be necessary to represent this term. Alternate translation: [You see,]

The author is speaking as if the **kingdom** of Israel had been going in a certain direction and Yahweh **turned** it and made it go in a different direction. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he made David, the son of Jesse, rule the kingdom instead]
